message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for this Monopoly turn.

I have five unmortgaged properties but no monopolies. I am short two greens and one light blue. I am short one brown. I paid $70 rent to p1.

p1 has an orange monopoly and is cash poor. p3 controls all four railroads and a pink monopoly. p4 owns the dark blue monopoly with heavy buildings. The bank still holds Baltic, Oriental, Kentucky, Atlantic, and Pennsylvania Avenue.

The greens are the win condition. Pennsylvania Avenue is needed to complete them.

p4 has heavy dark blue buildings but only $74 cash. They cannot build more immediately.

p3 can afford one house on each pink property.

One house on each pink property costs $70 to $80 in rent. Two houses would cost $200 to $220. Three houses would cost $550 to $600. I have enough cash to survive the pink threat but not to build heavily.

Standard orange rent for Tennessee with one house is $90, not the $70 I paid. The game state is being trusted as-is. The available actions are end_turn, propose_trade, and mortgage_property.

I cannot build or buy property this turn. I am considering a trade to complete the light blue monopoly. Vermont is mortgaged, so acquiring it would cost $55 to unmortgage plus interest. The greens remain the only viable path to victory.

Oriental Avenue costs $100. The light blue monopoly is too weak to threaten the dark blues or pinks. Completing the yellow monopoly would cost roughly $414 plus house construction, which is feasible but risky because p1 may not sell mortgaged Marvin Gardens. The brown pair is too weak to justify the investment. Acquiring a piece of another player's monopoly would not help me build.

Trading with p4 to break their dark blue monopoly would be ideal, but they own houses on both properties. I cannot force them to sell buildings first, so proposing a trade for Park Place or Boardwalk risks rejection. I should avoid invalid trades.

I will not propose trades for Park Place or Boardwalk because they have houses and the trade would likely be invalid. Breaking p3's pink monopoly would be a major win, but he just paid $400 for Virginia and will not sell it cheaply. I need to determine what offer he would accept.

I cannot offer p3 any property that would complete a set for him. He has no greens or yellows, so giving him Pacific and North Carolina would not help him build. He also lacks the pieces to finish the yellow monopoly.

Breaking his pink monopoly is the only meaningful trade target. He just paid $400 for Virginia, so he will not sell it cheaply. He may be willing to trade St. Charles or States for cash, since he has $719 and wants to build.

Offering p3 $500 would leave me with only $657. That is still too little to build on the greens, so I must land on Pennsylvania Avenue to complete the set. p1 has an orange monopoly with houses and only $165 cash. Seizing one of his orange properties will be difficult.

I am now considering trading with p1 for his mortgaged Marvin Gardens. I would need to pay $154 plus 10% interest to unmortgage it, and I still need to acquire Atlantic Avenue from the bank to complete the yellow monopoly. p1 has houses on his orange properties and only $165 cash, so he may be willing to accept a cash offer.

No trade can instantly give me a monopoly. I still need to land on the bank's Atlantic Avenue to complete the yellow set, and p4 could attack me before that happens.

Mortgaging is not an option. I have no debt and $1157 cash, so I will keep my properties unmortgaged.

Both a trade for Marvin Gardens and one for Vermont are speculative. I am weighing whether to end the turn or propose a strategic trade.

A mortgaged Marvin Gardens is worth roughly $140 to $200, but I cannot build on it yet. Paying that for a piece of an incomplete set is too risky while p4 holds three houses on Boardwalk. I must keep a large cash buffer because the Boardwalk rent is $1400.

I calculated my total liquidity at $1677, which is only about $277 above the $1400 Boardwalk rent. Spending cash on a trade would leave me too exposed. I should avoid large cash outlays this turn. I also checked whether p1 could complete a set with Connecticut and Vermont, but they still need Oriental Avenue from the bank.

I will not offer cash to p1 because that would let them build. A trade with p3 for a pink property would be rejected and reveal my strategy, so I will not propose it. No trade is clearly positive expected value without risking my Boardwalk survival cash.

I am now reconsidering a trade with p4 to break their dark blue monopoly. Acquiring both Boardwalk and Park Place would eliminate the $1400 three-house rent threat entirely, though it would require paying enough cash to force them to sell their houses first.

Selling all houses on the dark blue group would return $500 to p4. Afterward, Boardwalk would rent for only $100 and Park Place for $70, eliminating the lethal threat entirely. They would only do this if desperate for cash or if I overpay.

I will end the turn. I cannot afford to overpay for a dark blue piece that would leave me with no cash and no second property. I need to preserve my $1157 for the $320 purchase of Pennsylvania Avenue and as a buffer against the $1400 Boardwalk rent.

I am now considering a small cash offer for p1's mortgaged Marvin Gardens. Paying $50 to $100 would leave my liquidity around $1577, which still covers the $1400 Boardwalk rent. I am unsure if that is worth it while Atlantic Avenue remains in the bank.

Marvin Gardens would make Atlantic Avenue more valuable to me and a better block against p3 or p4. I should not pay more than about $100 to $150 for it, because paying $200 would leave only $77 above the $1400 Boardwalk rent. I am now considering whether to propose this trade, since p1 previously encouraged me to drain p3.

A concrete offer of $80 cash for p1's mortgaged Marvin Gardens is being weighed. Receiving a mortgaged property in a trade requires paying 10% interest immediately, but leaving it mortgaged is acceptable. This would bring me one step closer to the yellow monopoly, which is the best buildable set available besides the greens. The total cost to fully develop the yellow group would be roughly $1764.

Neither the yellow nor the green monopoly can be built to a lethal level before I might hit Boardwalk. The greens would still leave me with only about $237 above the $1400 rent. p4 has no other properties to mortgage, so he cannot build another house without selling his current houses first.

A cheap Marvin Gardens trade would leak my yellow-monopoly intent to p1, who could then raise prices or block Atlantic Avenue. I will not propose it and will keep my turn message short and neutral.
